user.title: LC Technology relay board
user.description: Set up the relay board by choosing the bus type, then the number of relays and digital inputs.

tcp.title: Board behind a Modbus TCP gateway

data_description.host: Address of the Modbus TCP gateway the board's RS-485 line is wired to.
data_description.unit_id: Modbus address of the board. Factory default is 255.
data_description.channels: 1, 2, 4 or 8 depending on the variant. The same count of inputs is exposed.

serial.title: Board on a serial port
serial.description: Integrations sharing one serial port share one connection, so every one of them must use the same baud rate, parity and stop bits.

data_description.device: The USB RS-485 adapter the board is wired to.
data_description.baudrate: As set on the board; the factory default is 9600.
data_description.unit_id: Modbus address of the board. Factory default is 255.
data_description.channels: 1, 2, 4 or 8 depending on the variant. The same count of inputs is exposed.

existing.title: Connection already in use
existing.description: Gateways and serial ports Home Assistant already talks to, with the integrations using them. The board shares that connection.

error.cannot_connect: The board did not answer. Check the gateway address, the unit ID and the wiring.
error.link_conflict: This gateway or port is already in use by another integration with different link settings.

data_description.channels: Lowering it removes the entities of the dropped channels.

update_failed.message: Could not read the relay board: {error}

pulse.name: Pulse
pulse.description: Turns a relay on and lets the board turn it off again after the duration. The board times the pulse itself, so it ends even if the connection drops.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long the relay stays on, in seconds (0.1 s resolution).
